candidates.rule: On November 3 at 21:46, the user set the shop stock cap to 50% of starting funds, to refill sold stock, and to keep the first-visit-at-cost offer; the later November 17 sell-down plan does not change that cap.
candidates.quote: stock cap back to 50% of the start, refill what sold; first visit at cost kept
candidates.harness: Cap restocking at 50% of starting funds, refill sold items, and retain the first-visit-at-cost offer only until the scheduled November 4 strategy change.

candidates.rule: At the first buying window, 22 product lines were purchased in six minutes, about one line every ten seconds, while buyers reported no stock.
candidates.quote: first window bought 22 lines in 6 min (one line per ~10 s) while buyers got 'none in stock'
candidates.harness: Track whether restocking provides enough units per product line to serve buyers, rather than treating a purchased line as sufficient stock.

candidates.rule: The first buying window showed that restocking a line with several units stocks more than buying one unit per line.
candidates.quote: restock's situation now says a line of several units stocks more
candidates.harness: Prefer multiple units per selected line when restocking.

candidates.rule: The board counts shop profit as current balance minus starting balance, with stock valued at zero.
candidates.quote: the board counts shop profit as balance - start with stock at zero
candidates.harness: Calculate or monitor shop score using balance minus starting balance; do not count remaining stock as value.

candidates.rule: On November 3 at 21:46, shop ALL fell from 0.569 to 0.409 after stock was filled, with reported profit of -1.56M; stock was 2.44M against the 2.5M cap.
candidates.quote: shop ALL fell 0.569 -> 0.409 (profit -1.56M) while v6 filled the stock; stock 2.44M of the 2.5M cap at install
candidates.harness: Account for the score impact of spending on inventory whose value is not counted by the board.

candidates.rule: The November 3 buyer strategy accepts useful zero-surplus deals and grade B goods, and does not ask for a warranty on food.
candidates.quote: buyer takes useful zero-surplus deals, accepts grade B, no warranty asked on food
candidates.harness: Allow useful zero-surplus purchases and grade B; do not request a food warranty.

candidates.rule: The shop's “No food” line refers to the shop's stock, not a buyer rule; the buyer previously misread it and walked away from food orders.
candidates.quote: the shop's 'No food' line now says it is about our stock (the buyer had read it as its own rule and walked from food orders)
candidates.harness: Interpret “No food” as a statement about the shop's stock, not a restriction on the buyer.

candidates.rule: On November 3 at 21:46, the user changed the returning buyer's minimum acceptable payment to the list price; on November 3 at 22:25, the user lowered it to 90% of list.
candidates.quote: a returning buyer may pay down to 90% of list
candidates.harness: Allow the returning buyer to pay as low as 90% of list price; do not enforce the superseded list-price floor.

candidates.rule: After the list-price floor took effect, the shop made one sale in 25 minutes after 21:59, compared with 13 sales in the preceding 30 minutes; nearly every returning buyer offered 90% of list and walked away.
candidates.quote: 1 sale in 25 min after 21:59 (13 in the 30 min before): nearly every buyer had dealt with us, rose to 90% of list and walked
candidates.harness: Avoid requiring returning buyers to pay full list price; use the 90%-of-list floor.

candidates.rule: The November 3 at 22:08 restocking strategy prioritizes SKUs buyers requested, then SKUs in requested categories priced near the median, and excludes categories nobody requested; it set eight units per SKU.
candidates.quote: restock's candidates are the SKUs buyers asked us for first
candidates.harness: Prioritize requested SKUs, then requested categories near median price; exclude unrequested categories and stock eight units per selected SKU unless a later strategy overrides the quantity.

candidates.rule: The most-requested SKUs recorded on November 3 at 22:10 were mattress G0f415407 with 55 asks, bedding Ge62449c9 with 27, and sofa Gaae7863f with 14.
candidates.quote: mattress 55, Ge62449c9 bedding 27, Gaae7863f sofa 14
candidates.harness: Use these recorded request counts as dated demand observations, not as permanent demand values.

candidates.rule: A cheapest-first restock trial selected spray paint and gum from noisy catalog categories and was dropped.
candidates.quote: a cheapest-first try picked spray paint and gum from noisy catalog categories and was dropped
candidates.harness: Do not use cheapest-first selection across noisy catalog categories as the restocking rule.

candidates.rule: The November 3 at 22:37 strategy puts requested SKUs first, then stocks best sellers deeply using the shop's goods and then the market's goods.
candidates.quote: restock holds the best sellers deep (ours, then the market's goods) after the SKUs buyers asked for
candidates.harness: Prioritize requested SKUs, then maintain deeper stock of best sellers from the shop's goods before market goods.

candidates.rule: The user scheduled restocking to stop at November 17 at 12:00 so the shop can sell down its stock before the Round 3 market closes.
candidates.quote: restock stops buying at 11/17 12:00 to sell the stock down
candidates.harness: Stop buying stock at November 17, 12:00.

candidates.rule: The November 3 at 22:37 buyer strategy aims at 55% of list on goods orders with list price at least 50,000, opens near 45%, and accepts any ask below list before turns run out.
candidates.quote: buyer aims at 55% of list on goods orders of list 50,000+ (open near 45%, take any ask under list before the turns run out)
candidates.harness: For goods orders listed at 50,000 or more, open near 45% of list, target 55%, and accept an ask below list if turns are running out.

candidates.rule: The November 3 at 22:37 buyer strategy prefers shops that show a warranty.
candidates.quote: prefers shops showing a warranty
candidates.harness: Prefer shops displaying a warranty when choosing among shops.

candidates.rule: The completed-order median buyer speed was 32 seconds; the observed gap to top buyers was in orders received, not time per order.
candidates.quote: median 32 s per completed order; the gap to the top buyers is in orders received, not time per order
candidates.harness: Leave buyer speed unchanged; focus on receiving more orders rather than reducing time per completed order.

candidates.rule: The shop's buy checks and restocking must preserve a reserve equal to 50% of sales still under warranty, in addition to the cash floor.
candidates.quote: check.buy and restock keep 50% of our sales still in warranty above the cash floor
candidates.harness: Maintain the required 50% warranty reserve above the cash floor when checking purchases and restocking.

candidates.rule: On November 3, the ledger showed 24 sales and 1.88M still open under warranty, with no ledger break observed at that point.
candidates.quote: 24 sales, 1.88M open, no break on the ledger yet
candidates.harness: Monitor open warranty exposure and ledger consistency; treat these figures as a dated observation.

candidates.rule: Only forum posts citing a settlement line such as “Settled SKU=.. price=..; grade=..” receive votes; posts without supporting settlement references received none.
candidates.quote: only posts like 'Settled SKU=.. price=..; grade=..' with the ledger settle line under them get votes
candidates.harness: Require a cited ledger settlement line for settlement-based forum posts.

candidates.rule: Forum posting must refuse posts without a cited fact and refuse numbers that do not appear in the cited lines; the cited lines are appended to the post.
candidates.quote: act.post refuses a post without one, refuses numbers not in the cited lines, and appends the lines itself
candidates.harness: Validate each post against its cited fact, reject unsupported numbers, and include the cited lines.

candidates.rule: The own-post vote guard failed because the market's post response uses {"post": id}, while the collector expected a different shape and recorded no IDs.
candidates.quote: own_posts read the market's {"post": id} answer as no id
candidates.harness: Read the post ID from the market's {"post": id} response so the own-post vote guard can work.

candidates.rule: At the November 3 21:2x board snapshot, buyer ALL was 0.18 versus a median of 0.479, and buyer posts and their votes accounted for 40% of buyer ALL.
candidates.quote: buyer ALL 0.18 vs median 0.479, 0 buyer posts - posts and their votes are 40% of buyer ALL
candidates.harness: Treat buyer forum activity as score-relevant; the recorded 40% contribution is a dated board observation.

candidates.rule: The forum side with fewer posts writes next and cites a settlement of its own: the buyer cites its payments and the shop cites its sales.
candidates.quote: the side with fewer posts writes next and cites a settle of its own (buyer: our payments, shop: our sales)
candidates.harness: Have the side with fewer posts take the next posting turn and cite its own qualifying settlement.

candidates.rule: Each forum turn posts once as buyer and once as shop; the kit allows one post per five minutes per side.
candidates.quote: each forum turn posts once as buyer and once as shop (the kit allows one per 5 min per side)
candidates.harness: Post at most once per side per five minutes, and use each forum turn for both buyer and shop posting when allowed.

candidates.rule: Besides settlement posts, the buyer may post unserved order needs with category and budget, and the shop may post held stock with SKU, units, grade, list price, certificate, and warranty; replies to goods requests belong in their threads.
candidates.quote: the buyer may post what we need (our orders no shop could serve: category, budget) and the shop what it holds (SKU, units, grade, list price, certificate, warranty)
candidates.harness: Support need and stock posts with the specified facts, and reply to goods requests in the requesting thread.

candidates.rule: The Round 3 collector initially counted each sale twice: paid deals have a settlement line and a result line, while an unpaid receipt also has a result line.
candidates.quote: a paid deal has a settle line and a result line, and an unpaid receipt has a result line too
candidates.harness: Do not count both settlement and result lines as separate sales.

candidates.rule: The verified Round 3 result lines showed 27 paid sales totaling 1,902,300, matching the board; 59 seller.settled records had been collected, and the brief's 57 deals and 2.28M revenue were inflated.
candidates.quote: 59 seller.settled for 27 paid sales (= the board's 27, sum 1,902,300)
candidates.harness: Use verified paid-sale results and reconcile sales totals with the board; do not use the inflated 57-deal or 2.28M figures.

candidates.rule: Round 3 sale counting uses only the verified result line, which carries price, task, and stars; map each sale's result sequence number to the settlement line for its order.
candidates.quote: Round 3 now counts only the verified result line (it carries price, task and stars); forum maps a sale's result seq to the settle line of its order
candidates.harness: Count verified result lines once, retain their price, task, and stars, and link them to the corresponding order settlement for forum citations.

candidates.rule: Earlier sale events remained recorded as they were before the Round 3 counting fix.
candidates.quote: earlier events stay as recorded
candidates.harness: Do not silently rewrite earlier recorded events when applying the corrected counting rule.

candidates.rule: On November 3 at 22:35, the live run was snapshotted before moving it to the home PC; the kit log showed 31 shop settlements and a balance of 3,009,784.
candidates.quote: 11/3 22:35 (31 shop settles in the kit log, balance 3,009,784) before moving the run to the home PC
candidates.harness: Preserve the dated live-run snapshot and reconcile it when moving or resuming the run.

candidates.rule: The November 3 at 22:37 strategy ends the first-visit-at-cost offer at the November 4 00:00 activation of v13; thereafter every buyer starts from list price and may pay down to 90% of list.
candidates.quote: v13 ends the first-visit-at-cost offer (every buyer from list, down to 90%)
candidates.harness: At the scheduled v13 activation, stop offering first-visit-at-cost prices and allow every buyer to negotiate from list down to 90%.
